items.headline: SPIE to acquire 76% stake in Austrian industrial services firm SAR Anlagenbau
items.parties: Acquirer: SPIE SA; Target: SAR ANLAGENBAU GmbH (76% stake)
items.take: SPIE signed an agreement to acquire a 76% stake in SAR ANLAGENBAU GmbH of Hausmening, Austria, which has about 230 employees and around €100 million of revenue for fiscal 2025/26. Managing director Arno Reisinger will hold up to 24%, closing is expected at the beginning of 2027, and the price was not disclosed.

items.headline: Platinum Equity to acquire propane distributor EDP
items.parties: Acquirer: Platinum Equity; Target: EDP
items.take: Platinum Equity signed a definitive agreement to acquire Chicago-based EDP, which serves more than 200,000 customers through more than 60 locations in 24 states. The deal is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, and no closing date was stated.

items.headline: Franklin Electric to acquire Challenge Pumps for about US$181M cash
items.parties: Acquirer: Franklin Electric; Target: Challenge Pumps Holdings Pty Ltd
items.value_text: About US$181M cash (A$259M) plus up to US$14M contingent consideration
items.take: Franklin Electric agreed to acquire Perth-based underground mine dewatering provider Challenge Pumps for about US$181 million in cash, plus up to US$14 million contingent on post-closing revenue. The release cites FY2026 revenue of about US$52 million and expects closing in 2026, subject to the target's audit and customary conditions.

items.headline: Renasant to acquire Commercial Holding Company in stock deal valued at about $142M
items.parties: Acquirer: Renasant Corporation; Target: Commercial Holding Company (parent of Commercial Bank & Trust Company)
items.value_text: About $142M (0.8798 Renasant shares per Commercial share)
items.take: Renasant will issue 0.8798 shares per Commercial share, about 2.64 million shares in total, valued at about $142 million at a $40.29 ten-day average price. Commercial had about $1.1 billion in total assets at September 30, 2026; closing is expected in Q1 2027 pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.

items.headline: La Caisse to buy 49.9% of Bell wireless tower company TowerCo for C$2.45B
items.parties: Acquirer: La Caisse; Target: 49.9% stake in TowerCo (Bell Canada, retains 50.1%)
items.value_text: C$2.45B for a 49.9% stake (about C$4.91B implied TowerCo value)
items.take: La Caisse will pay C$2.45 billion, subject to customary adjustments, for 49.9% of a newly formed Bell wireless tower company, which the release says values it at about C$4.91 billion. Bell retains a 50.1% controlling interest and closing is expected in Q1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.headline: ENEOS Holdings completes acquisition of TPC Group
items.parties: Acquirer: ENEOS Holdings, Inc.; Target: TPC Group
items.take: TPC Group announced the completion of its acquisition by ENEOS Holdings, Inc. in a release dated Oct. 27, 2026. The release excerpt reviewed does not state a purchase price.

items.headline: Ares Capital to acquire MidCap Financial Investment Corporation
items.parties: Acquirer: Ares Capital Corporation; Target: MidCap Financial Investment Corporation
items.take: Ares Capital agreed to acquire MFIC for total consideration of $10.88 per fully diluted share, about $1.21 in cash and about $9.67 in Ares Capital stock. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to MFIC stockholder and regulatory approvals.
items.source_name: Ares Capital press release (SEC Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)

items.headline: Guidewire to acquire hyperexponential for $1.7B cash plus up to $400M contingent
items.parties: Acquirer: Guidewire; Target: hyperexponential
items.value_text: $1.7B base cash plus up to $400M contingent
items.take: Guidewire signed a definitive agreement to acquire London-based hyperexponential for a base price of $1.7 billion in cash plus up to $400 million contingent on recurring revenue targets. Funding is $1.0 billion of new term loan plus existing cash; closing is expected in Guidewire fiscal Q2 2027.

items.headline: RadNet to acquire ONRAD for $350M cash plus 5M shares; earnout up to $210M
items.parties: Acquirer: RadNet, Inc.; Target: ONRAD, Inc.
items.value_text: $350M cash plus 5M RadNet shares; earnout up to $210M
items.take: ONRAD provides teleradiology and in-hospital professional radiology staffing, with more than 130 contracted radiologists supporting more than 225 hospital facilities across 26 states. RadNet expects it to add $190M-$200M of revenue in its first year after closing, which is expected in early 2027.

items.headline: Acuity to acquire Parameter Technologies for $675M purchase price
items.parties: Acquirer: Acuity Inc.; Target: Parameter Technologies
items.take: Acuity agreed to buy Parameter Technologies (RLE Technologies and CellWatch brands), which provides leak detection and environmental and battery monitoring for data centers and critical infrastructure. It will fund the deal with $500 million of borrowings and balance-sheet cash; closing is expected in Q2 of fiscal 2027, subject to HSR.

items.headline: Truelink Capital to acquire Johnson Controls' global intrusion products business
items.parties: Acquirer: Truelink Capital; Seller: Johnson Controls; Target: Global intrusion products business
items.take: Truelink Capital signed a definitive agreement for the business behind the DSC, Qolsys, PowerG, Visonic, Bentel and Sur-Gard brands; financial terms were not disclosed. Closing is expected in the first half of calendar 2027, and the business is to operate as a standalone company.

items.headline: Umios to acquire High Liner Foods for C$27.00 per share in cash
items.parties: Acquirer: Umios Corporation; Target: High Liner Foods Incorporated
items.take: Umios agreed to buy High Liner for C$27.00 per share in cash, about C$804 million in equity value, funded mainly with interest-bearing debt and cash on hand. Completion is expected in January 2027, subject to a 75% shareholder vote, Competition Act and HSR clearance; holders of about 45.4% have signed voting support agreements.

items.headline: Third Coast Bancshares to acquire Great Plains Bancshares in all-stock deal
items.parties: Acquirer: Third Coast Bancshares, Inc.; Target: Great Plains Bancshares, Inc.
items.value_text: ~$239.6 million all-stock, based on Oct. 6 closing price
items.take: Third Coast expects to issue 5,570,352 shares, leaving Third Coast holders with about 78% and Great Plains holders about 22% of the combined company. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and shareholder votes at both companies.

items.headline: Acuity to acquire Parameter Technologies for $675M
items.parties: Acquirer: Acuity Inc.; Target: Parameter Technologies
items.take: Acuity said it reached a definitive agreement to buy Parameter, which makes leak, environmental and battery monitoring products for data centers, utilities and critical infrastructure. It will fund the deal with $500 million of borrowings plus cash, with closing expected in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino expiration.

items.headline: EQT to acquire Range Resources in all-stock deal; pro forma EV over $50B
items.parties: Acquirer: EQT Corp; Target: Range Resources Corp
items.value_text: All-stock; 0.987 EQT shares per Range share (no dollar price stated; combined pro forma EV over $50B)
items.take: Each Range share will be exchanged for 0.987 EQT shares, leaving Range holders with about 27% of the combined company. EQT expects $325 million of base annual synergies within two years and closing in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
items.source_name: EQT Corp. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1 press release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Ovintiv to acquire Logan Energy for C$1.40 per share in cash; about US$890M
items.parties: Acquirer: Ovintiv Inc.; Target: Logan Energy Corp.
items.value_text: About C$1.26B (about US$890M), including Logan's expected net debt at closing
items.take: Ovintiv will fund the all-cash deal from cash on hand, credit facility borrowings and commercial paper, and Logan will spin out Logan Oil Corp. to its shareholders. Closing is expected early in Q1 2027, subject to Logan shareholder, court and regulatory approvals.
items.source_name: Ovintiv Inc. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1 press release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Corxel US to go public via business combination with Amanat Acquisition Corp
items.parties: SPAC: Amanat Acquisition Corp; Target: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Corxel US)
items.value_text: Undisclosed valuation; about $377M expected gross proceeds (about $75M trust plus about $300M PIPE)
items.take: The combined company is expected to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market under a new name and ticker, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. The release says proceeds are expected to support the company through 2029; the $377M assumes no Amanat shareholder redemptions.
items.source_name: Corxel US and Amanat Acquisition Corp release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: eQ Plc to acquire Genesta Property Nordic
items.parties: Acquirer: eQ Plc; Target: Genesta Property Nordic AB; Sellers: Caprock Ventures AB, Philip Björk Invest II AB, Pinetwig AB, Ted Söderlund Invest AB
items.value_text: Up to EUR 15.5M debt-free (EUR 11.5M base + up to EUR 4.0M earn-out)
items.take: eQ agreed to acquire Genesta, a Nordic real estate asset manager with approximately EUR 1 billion in assets across three funds. Base price is EUR 11.5M (about half cash, half new eQ shares) and closing is expected at the latest in Q1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
items.source_name: eQ Plc inside information release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Dayforce to acquire Ribbon AI
items.parties: Acquirer: Dayforce, Inc.; Target: Ribbon AI Inc.
items.take: Dayforce signed an agreement to acquire Ribbon AI, an AI recruiting technology company. The release does not state terms or an expected closing date.

items.headline: Lycia Therapeutics prices upsized IPO at $18.00 per share, about $317.5M gross
items.parties: Issuer: Lycia Therapeutics; Underwriters: Jefferies, TD Cowen, Evercore ISI, Guggenheim Securities (joint book-runners)
items.take: Lycia priced 17,640,000 shares at $18.00, with a 30-day underwriter option for up to 2,646,000 more shares. Trading on Nasdaq Global Select under "LYCA" was expected to begin Oct. 23, with closing expected Oct. 26.

items.headline: CRH completes acquisition of Arcosa; total enterprise value about $8.5B
items.parties: Acquirer: CRH; Target: Arcosa, Inc.
items.take: CRH said on Oct. 23, 2026 that it has completed its acquisition of Arcosa under the agreement dated June 22, 2026. It will update full-year 2026 guidance for the deal with its third-quarter results on Oct. 29.

items.headline: Zymeworks licenses DLL3 T cell engager ZW209 to Roche; $55M upfront
items.parties: Licensor: Zymeworks Inc.; Licensee: Roche
items.value_text: $55M upfront; $40M on Phase 1b initiation; up to $718M in further milestones
items.take: Roche receives the exclusive global right to develop and commercialize ZW209, and Zymeworks keeps eligibility for milestones and tiered royalties from high-single-digit to mid-teen percentages on net sales. Roche funds the Phase 1a trial, and the agreement is conditioned on expiration or termination of the HSR Act waiting period.

items.headline: Gilead to acquire PepStar's oral IL-23R inhibitor HCXT-2001 for $1.275B cash
items.parties: Acquirer: Gilead Sciences, Inc.; Target: PepStar Therapeutics Limited (HCXT-2001 program)
items.value_text: $1.275B cash at closing, subject to customary adjustments; no milestones stated
items.take: Gilead is acquiring an oral macrocyclic peptide IL-23R inhibitor that is in Phase 1 clinical trials, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Gilead expects the transaction to reduce GAAP and non-GAAP EPS by approximately $0.79 to $0.83.

items.headline: Investors buy 50% of Oro Mobility voting units from Hertz for about $80.9M
items.parties: Acquirer: Cohen Private Ventures and funds affiliated with Certares and/or Knighthead; Seller: The Hertz Corporation; Target: Oro Mobility Holdings LLC
items.value_text: About $80.89M cash for Class A units (about 15.86% of common units; 50% of voting units)
items.take: The investors' purchase closed October 19, 2026, after Hertz contributed Oro business assets and about $60.03 million of cash to the entity. Hertz also agreed to repurchase about $51.1 million principal of its 2029 exchangeable notes from certain investor affiliates for about $20.86 million.

items.headline: Cencora agrees to acquire remaining equity of American Oncology Network; EV $2.4B
items.parties: Acquirer: Cencora; Target: American Oncology Network
items.value_text: Enterprise value $2.4B ($2.3B at closing plus CVRs of up to $100M)
items.take: Cencora, which holds about 4%, agreed to acquire all equity it does not own; assuming a 25% stockholder rollover it expects to pay about $1.7B to reach 75%. Closing is subject to regulatory clearances and AON stockholder approval.

items.headline: Merck KGaA to acquire Silence Therapeutics for $20.00 per ADS in cash, about $1.3B
items.parties: Acquirer: Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany; Target: Silence Therapeutics plc
items.value_text: About $1.3B equity value ($20.00 per ADS in cash); enterprise value $1.1B
items.take: The $20.00 per-ADS cash price is a 130% premium to the Oct. 16 close and 82% above the 30-day VWAP of $10.99. Holders of about 14% of the voting power signed a support agreement; closing is expected in Q1 2027.

items.headline: Cognizant to acquire DyFlex Solutions, an Australia-based SAP Platinum Partner
items.parties: Acquirer: Cognizant; Target: DyFlex Solutions
items.take: DyFlex was founded in 2011, has over 300 people and provides SAP advisory, implementation and managed services across Australia and New Zealand. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.headline: TTM Technologies to acquire MKS's Ophir Optics business for about $650M
items.parties: Acquirer: TTM Technologies, Inc.; Target: Ophir Optics business of MKS Inc.
items.value_text: Approx. $650M all-cash, subject to customary closing adjustments
items.take: TTM would pay approximately $650 million in cash, roughly 10.3x expected FY 2027 Adjusted EBITDA of Ophir Optics without synergies. Closing is expected in the second quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions.

items.headline: Salesforce to acquire Braze for $47.50 per share in cash
items.parties: Acquirer: Salesforce, Inc.; Target: Braze, Inc.
items.value_text: $47.50 per share in cash; enterprise value approx. $5.66B
items.take: Braze Class A holders would receive $47.50 in cash per share, at an enterprise value of approximately $5.66 billion. Closing is expected in Salesforce's fiscal 2028, subject to Braze shareholder approval and regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Maximus to acquire Agile Defense for $660M cash plus up to $50M earnout
items.parties: Acquirer: Maximus Federal Services, Inc. (subsidiary of Maximus, Inc.); Target: Agile Defense, LLC; Seller: Arclight Equity Holdings, LLC
items.take: The $660 million cash price is reduced by Agile Defense's indebtedness and certain transaction expenses, with up to $50 million more tied to revenue milestones in the 12 months after closing. Closing is expected in Maximus's fiscal first quarter of 2027 and requires no shareholder approval.

items.headline: International Seaways to buy VLCC owner Bruton, valued at about $370M
items.parties: Acquirer: International Seaways, Inc.; Target: Bruton Limited
items.take: International Seaways signed agreements on October 16 to acquire Bruton, valued at approximately $370 million, starting with a first-step exchange of about 50.5% of Bruton's shares at 0.05190 INSW shares per Bruton share (expected to settle on or about October 20), followed by a merger for the rest; holders of 10,000 or fewer shares receive $6.3044 cash per share, and Seaways expects to issue about 3.12 million shares in total. The deal adds four VLCCs including newbuildings, and with exchanging holders committed to vote for the merger, the Bruton shareholder meeting expected around October 30 is the main remaining step.

items.headline: City Therapeutics prices upsized $200M Nasdaq IPO at $18 a share
items.parties: Issuer: City Therapeutics, Inc.; Joint bookrunners: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Jefferies, Stifel, Oppenheimer & Co.
items.take: City Therapeutics priced an upsized IPO of 11,111,111 shares at $18.00 for gross proceeds of about $200.0 million, with trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under CTY set to begin October 16 and closing expected October 19; underwriters have a 30-day option on up to 1,666,666 more shares. The clinical-stage RNAi developer, whose lead programs target thromboembolic disease, Stargardt and other retinal diseases, and anemia of chronic disease, adds to a busy run of biotech listings this month.

items.headline: Strive prices upsized $630M IPO of 15% perpetual SATS preferred stock
items.parties: Issuer: Strive, Inc.; Joint bookrunners: Barclays Capital Inc., Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.; Lead manager: Clear Street LLC
items.take: Strive's final term sheet prices 7,000,000 shares of 15.00% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock at $90.00 each, upsized from 5,000,000, for gross proceeds of about $630 million; each share carries an initial $100 liquidation preference, settlement is set for October 20, and Strive has applied to list on Nasdaq as SATS. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes including the acquisition of bitcoin, so this is a high-coupon preferred being used to fund a bitcoin treasury strategy.
items.source_name: Strive pricing term sheet, Form FWP (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Scanntech raises $180M Series F led by L Catterton, Partners Group
items.parties: Lead: L Catterton; Co-lead: Partners Group (on behalf of its clients); Participants: Bradesco, SPX
items.take: Uruguay-founded Scanntech, a retail intelligence platform for consumer goods in Latin America, announced a $180 million Series F led by L Catterton with Partners Group as co-lead and Bradesco and SPX participating, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Its direct point-of-sale data covers more than 80% of retail sell-out in its markets, and the new money is earmarked for analytics and AI, new products and new markets.

items.headline: Transocean lifts revolver to $750M, extends maturity to October 2031
items.parties: Borrower: Transocean International Limited (Transocean Ltd. subsidiary); Administrative and collateral agent: Citibank, N.A.
items.take: Transocean's subsidiary signed an amended and restated credit agreement that raises revolving commitments to $750 million from $510 million and pushes scheduled maturity from June 2028 to October 2031, effective upon customary conditions and the closing of Transocean's acquisition of Valaris. Transocean also said it retired $165 million of 8.00% Deepwater Aquila senior secured notes due 2028 on October 1, which it expects to save about $22 million of interest through maturity.
items.source_name: Transocean press release, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

items.headline: Daily Journal buys AI evidence-software maker Revir Technologies for cash
items.parties: Acquirer: Daily Journal Corporation; Target: Revir Technologies, Inc.
items.take: Daily Journal completed its acquisition of Austin-based Revir Technologies on October 13, funding it with cash on hand and describing it as not material; Revir's Scout platform uses AI to help law enforcement, prosecutors and courts manage and search large volumes of digital evidence. Revir will run independently inside the courts, justice and government technology division alongside Journal Technologies, extending that unit's case-management offering.

items.headline: Lufthansa picked to buy 44.9% of TAP Air Portugal for €1.025B
items.parties: Acquirer: Lufthansa Group; Target: TAP Air Portugal (minority stake); Process run by: Portuguese government and Parpública
items.take: Portugal's government selected Lufthansa Group's offer in the TAP privatization: EUR 1.025 billion for a 44.9 percent stake, rising to up to EUR 1.2 billion for 49.9 percent to reflect shares first offered to employees and a ticking fee, with signing expected shortly and completion subject to regulatory approval. Lufthansa gains a minority foothold in TAP and its Atlantic network, and the remaining regulatory reviews are the main hurdle before closing.

items.headline: Skeleton Technologies tops $1B valuation in nine-figure round led by Siemens
items.parties: Lead: Siemens; Company: Skeleton Technologies
items.take: Skeleton Technologies says a nine-figure investment round led by Siemens brings its valuation to more than $1 billion, with proceeds mainly for expanding its U.S. manufacturing footprint and plans to invest more than $200 million in operational scale-up and R&D in Silicon Valley. A strategic lead from Siemens ties Skeleton's supercapacitor and power-system technology more closely to a major data-center equipment supplier, though the exact size of the round was not disclosed.

items.headline: Hulic launches ¥295-a-share tender offer to take Riso Kyoiku private
items.parties: Acquirer: Hulic Co., Ltd.; Target: RISO KYOIKU GROUP CORPORATION
items.value_text: ¥295 per share cash tender offer; total undisclosed
items.take: Hulic, which already holds 50.87% of Riso Kyoiku Group, is tendering at 295 yen per share from October 14 to November 26, 2026, with a minimum of 26,646,601 shares, aiming to make the company a wholly owned subsidiary and delist it. The deal fits the steady wave of Japanese parent-subsidiary take-privates, where majority holders buy out minorities to simplify listed group structures.
items.source_name: Riso Kyoiku Group tender offer announcement

items.headline: Nokia to sell Enterprise Campus Edge private-wireless unit to AURELIUS
items.parties: Acquirer: AURELIUS; Seller: Nokia; Target: Enterprise Campus Edge (ECE) business
items.take: Nokia signed a definitive agreement to sell its Enterprise Campus Edge business, which serves nearly 900 customers across manufacturing, mining, logistics, airports, ports and power generation, to AURELIUS, with closing expected in the first half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. The carve-out lets Nokia narrow its portfolio while handing a specialist private-wireless unit to a buyer focused on corporate spin-offs.

items.headline: Tenable closes new $400M secured revolver maturing 2031, initially undrawn
items.parties: Borrower: Tenable; Administrative agent: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.
items.take: Tenable entered a $400.0 million senior secured revolving credit facility, initially undrawn and maturing October 13, 2031, which completes the refinancing of its prior credit agreement including its Term Loan B and replaces a revolver that matured in July. Swapping term debt for an undrawn revolver gives the company liquidity flexibility without adding funded borrowings.

items.headline: Albert raises $55M Series B led by TCV for chemistry-native AI
items.parties: Lead: TCV; Participants: Delta-v Capital, Socium Ventures, HighSage Ventures, Coral Capital, Legion VC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners, Index Ventures, Applied Ventures, LLC
items.take: Albert, which says it built the first chemistry-native AI operating system for R&D, raised a $55 million Series B led by TCV with new and existing investors including Coatue, Index Ventures and Applied Ventures. The round shows growth investors backing vertical AI aimed at shortening materials and chemical development cycles.

items.headline: French AI accounting platform Dougs raises €50M from Expedition Growth Capital
items.parties: Lead: Expedition Growth Capital; Company: Dougs
items.take: Dougs, which serves more than 50,000 businesses and generates more than €50 million in annual recurring revenue, raised €50 million from existing backer Expedition Growth Capital to expand its AI and automation technology and broaden into legal and financial management. The company is targeting €100 million of ARR and 100,000 customers, a sign of growth capital flowing to profitable-scale European SMB software.

items.headline: Jio Platforms files RHP for IPO of up to 270M new shares; bidding opens Oct. 21
items.parties: Issuer: Jio Platforms Limited
items.value_text: Fresh issue of up to 270,000,000 shares (amount not stated in RHP)
items.take: Jio Platforms' red herring prospectus, dated October 14, 2026, covers a fresh issue of up to 270,000,000 equity shares with no offer for sale, anchor bidding on October 19 and a public bid window of October 21-23, with listing planned on BSE and NSE through a syndicate of 19 book-running lead managers. An all-primary structure means every rupee raised goes to the company rather than to existing holders, and the offering will test how deep Indian and global demand runs for one of the country's largest private digital platforms.

items.headline: TKO makes $2.0B all-cash offer for Service Properties Trust's hotel portfolio
items.parties: Bidder: TKO LLC; Target: Service Properties Trust (hospitality portfolio)
items.take: TKO LLC said it submitted a written letter of intent dated October 7 to buy Service Properties Trust's hospitality portfolio for $2.0 billion in cash, says it has received no meaningful response, and offered to deposit $50 million into escrow once SVC countersigns a non-disclosure agreement. The offer is a public pressure campaign rather than an agreed deal, and SVC's board has not endorsed it.

items.headline: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II prices $100M SPAC IPO at $10 a share, no warrants
items.parties: Issuer: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II; Sole book-runner: Guggenheim Securities
items.take: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II priced 10,000,000 Class A ordinary shares at $10.00 for $100 million in gross proceeds, with trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under TCXB from October 16 and closing expected on or about October 19; the offering carries no warrants and no over-allotment option. The shares-only structure and a stated focus on life sciences and medtech targets set it apart from the warrant-heavy SPAC template.
items.source_name: TCGX Acquisition Corp. II press release (Business Wire)

items.headline: Distribution Solutions Group to buy GradeEight Holdings for about $145M
items.parties: Acquirer: Lawson Products, Inc. (Distribution Solutions Group); Target: GradeEight Holdings, LLC
items.take: DSG's Lawson Products agreed on October 12 to acquire GradeEight Holdings, operator of Winzer and FastServ Supply with about $110 million in annual sales, for approximately $145 million, funded from DSG's $400 million revolver and cash with no financing condition and closing expected in the fourth quarter. The bolt-on lands while DSG itself is pending a going-private merger with LKCM Headwater affiliates, which hold about 78.5% of its stock.

items.headline: TheRealReal lands $150M Fortress term loan plus $25M revolver to retire 2029 notes
items.parties: Borrower: The RealReal, Inc.; Agent: Fortress Credit Corp.
items.take: TheRealReal entered a credit agreement with Fortress Credit Corp. as agent for a $150 million senior secured term loan at adjusted Term SOFR plus 5.75% and a $25 million revolver, using the term loan and cash to redeem in full its 4.25%/8.75% PIK/cash senior secured notes due 2029; the company expects about $4 million of first-year interest savings. Swapping a 13% all-in coupon for cash-pay floating debt pushes maturities to 2033 and cleans up a key overhang on the balance sheet.

items.headline: Salesforce signs deal to acquire AI analytics platform Loops; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Salesforce; Target: Loops
items.take: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Loops, an AI-powered analytics platform that monitors business KPIs and explains why metrics move, with closing expected in early November in its fiscal 2027, subject to customary conditions. The tuck-in slots into Tableau and adds to Salesforce's agentic-analytics push.

items.headline: Proofpoint to acquire Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3B
items.parties: Acquirer: Proofpoint; Target: Varonis
items.take: Proofpoint agreed to buy Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3 billion, a 52% premium to the June 22 close before initial sale rumors; Thoma Bravo committed equity and secured debt financing commitments, Ontario Teachers' agreed to invest in Proofpoint, and closing is expected in the first half of 2027 subject to Varonis shareholder and regulatory approvals. The deal folds a listed data-security specialist into a sponsor-owned email and human-risk platform, extending the run of private-capital consolidation in security software.

items.headline: 26North to buy data-center equipment mover MEI from Olympus Partners; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: 26North Partners; Target: MEI Industrial Solutions; Seller: Olympus Partners
items.take: 26North, through its affiliates, agreed to acquire Dallas-based MEI Industrial Solutions from Olympus Partners; MEI rigs, moves, stores and installs heavy equipment for data center, semiconductor, EV and battery, aerospace and life-sciences customers, with 30 operating locations and nearly 2,500 employees, and closing is expected in Q4 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Buyers are paying for picks-and-shovels exposure to the data-center build-out, where specialized installation capacity sits closer to the bottleneck than the hardware itself.

items.headline: Nasdaq completes acquisition of LeveL Markets ATS; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Nasdaq; Target: LeveL Markets
items.take: Nasdaq completed its acquisition of LeveL Markets, an off-exchange equity venue that it says is the third-largest U.S. ATS by trading volume and grew average daily volume 56% in 2025; Nasdaq first took a minority stake in 2021, terms were not disclosed, and LeveL will keep operating as a FINRA-registered ATS. Owning a large dark pool lets Nasdaq capture flow that has been migrating off-exchange rather than ceding it to broker-run venues.

items.headline: Cronos completes €57.5M acquisition of Dutch cannabis producer CanAdelaar
items.parties: Acquirer: Cronos Group; Target: CanAdelaar
items.take: Cronos closed its purchase of CanAdelaar, the largest company in the Netherlands' adult-use cannabis pilot program, for a €57.5 million base price subject to adjustments plus contingent cash payments equal to 0.5x CanAdelaar's normalized EBITDA for each of 2026 and 2027. The EBITDA-linked earnout ties part of the price to how the Dutch pilot performs, giving Cronos a regulated European foothold without paying fully up front.

items.headline: Intuit to acquire AI-native revenue management platform Sequence; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Intuit; Target: Sequence
items.take: Intuit signed an agreement to acquire Sequence, a London- and New York-based Series A company founded in 2021 whose AI-native platform automates quote-to-revenue work from pricing and billing to collections and revenue recognition; financial terms were not disclosed. The buy plugs a mid-market revenue-operations gap for Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced, pushing Intuit further up-market against dedicated billing vendors.

items.headline: Battery-electrode printer Sakuu to go public via Pyrophyte II SPAC at $600M pre-money
items.parties: SPAC: Pyrophyte Acquisition Corp. II; Target: Sakuu Corporation
items.take: Sakuu, a Silicon Valley maker of Kavian dry-printing equipment for battery and supercapacitor electrodes, agreed to combine with Pyrophyte Acquisition Corp. II at an implied $600 million pre-money equity value, with the combined company expected to list on the NYSE as SAKU. The release names no PIPE or trust size and the deal still needs both companies' shareholder votes and an S-4, so the funding the combined company actually receives remains the open variable.

items.headline: Chubby Group raises $50M Series A at $500M valuation, signs LOI for 47 GEN BBQ sites
items.parties: Lead: Prysm Capital; Issuer: Chubby Group; LOI counterparty: GEN Restaurant Group
items.value_text: $50M Series A; GEN asset LOI valued at up to $100M
items.take: Chubby Group closed a $50 million Series A led by Prysm Capital at a $500 million valuation and signed a letter of intent to take over GEN Restaurant Group's 47 U.S. restaurants and four development sites in a deal valued at up to $100 million, with part of the consideration a note convertible into Chubby equity at a $1.5 billion valuation. Because the GEN piece is an LOI still needing definitive agreements and lease transfers, the near-term story is the fresh equity funding Chubby's expansion, with the GEN rollout a phased, conditional option.
items.correction: Clarified that the convertible note is part of the consideration for the GEN assets, not the full payment, per the release.

items.headline: Harmonic Security raises $50M Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners
items.parties: Lead: Crosspoint Capital Partners; Participants: existing investors
items.take: Harmonic Security, which helps organizations control and monitor employees' use of AI tools, raised a $50 million Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners with existing investors participating, bringing total funding to $76 million. The capital goes to engineering and go-to-market across the US and UK, a sign that AI-usage governance is graduating from pilot budgets into a funded security category.

items.headline: TNS acquires phone-number intelligence provider netnumber; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: TNS (Transaction Network Services); Target: netnumber
items.take: TNS announced the acquisition of netnumber, a provider of phone number intelligence and registry services spanning portability, routing and digital identity verification for customers in the US, Canada and more than 50 other countries; financial terms were not disclosed. The deal deepens TNS's fraud-prevention and routing stack as carriers face rising pressure to authenticate callers and numbers.

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to buy $330M of new Bending Spoons shares at $33 each
items.parties: Investor: Berkshire Hathaway; Issuer: Bending Spoons S.p.A.
items.take: Bending Spoons will issue 10 million new ordinary shares to Berkshire Hathaway at $33.00 each in a $330 million private placement, lifting Berkshire's total stake to 4% after its $600 million investment at the July 2026 IPO; the deal is subject to customary closing conditions. Management tied the cash to acquisition capacity, so the placement reads as a balance-sheet top-up for Bending Spoons' serial buy-and-integrate model rather than a passive stake.

items.headline: ICON raises $200M Series D co-led by Baillie Gifford and BlackRock funds
items.parties: Co-leads: Baillie Gifford, funds managed by BlackRock; Participants include: Capital Factory, CAZ Investments, Moderne Ventures, Moonshots Capital, Norwest, Overmatch, The Syndicate, Tiger Global
items.take: ICON raised a $200 million Series D to scale manufacturing and deployment of its robotic 3D-printing construction systems, build a large R&D facility in Austin and expand into new U.S. markets; it says it is on pace for 4x revenue growth in 2026 and has more than $370 million in government contracts through ICON Prime. Crossover backers leading the round suggest investors now see ICON's defense and housing contracts as a revenue base rather than a pilot program.

items.headline: Soufflé Therapeutics closes $135M Series B led by Juvia Group
items.parties: Lead: Juvia Group; New investors: TCG Crossover Management, BB Biotech, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Balyasny Asset Management, an unnamed sovereign wealth fund; Existing investors include: Amgen Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Leaps by Bayer, Polaris Partners, Temasek, Vida Ventures
items.take: Soufflé closed an oversubscribed $135 million Series B to fund first clinical studies in FSHD, heart failure (targeting phospholamban in cardiomyocytes) and a muscle and metabolic program with an undisclosed target. The arrival of crossover funds such as TCG Crossover and Fidelity alongside the venture syndicate is the usual signal that a company is being positioned for a public-market path once clinical data arrive.

items.headline: CVC Catalyst III to take minority stake in camouflage maker Fibrotex
items.parties: Investor: CVC Catalyst III fund (CVC); Target: Fibrotex; Majority owner: Blum family; Advisors: Rothschild (CVC), Jefferies (Blum family)
items.take: CVC agreed to invest in Fibrotex, a multispectral camouflage supplier with main locations in Kentucky and Petah Tikva, Israel, through its Catalyst III fund, with the founding Blum family keeping majority ownership; closing is expected in the first half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. A minority structure lets a large European sponsor gain defense exposure without taking control of a family-run supplier.

items.headline: GenNx360 closes ~$285M continuation fund for Whitsons, led by Churchill
items.parties: Sponsor: GenNx360 Capital Partners; Lead investor: Churchill Asset Management; Company: Whitsons Culinary Group; Financial advisor: Evercore
items.take: GenNx360 closed a single-asset continuation fund with about $285 million of total equity commitments for Whitsons Culinary Group, led by Churchill Asset Management, which is also a lender to the company; GenNx360 and management reinvested. Continuation vehicles like this let sponsors extend a hold on a growing asset, here one that has expanded from seven to 17 states, while offering existing LPs an option for liquidity.
items.source_name: GenNx360 Capital Partners press release (Business Wire)

items.headline: Duvo raises $32M Series A led by Balderton for enterprise AI operations
items.parties: Lead: Balderton Capital; Participants: Index Ventures, Northzone, Credo Ventures
items.take: Duvo raised a $32 million Series A led by Balderton, with existing investors Index Ventures, Northzone and Credo Ventures participating, bringing total funding to $48 million for its platform that runs business processes with people and AI agents across ERPs, supplier portals and spreadsheets. Investors are backing the pitch that AI agents earn their keep in governed back-office workflows, where savings can be measured, rather than in chat interfaces.

items.headline: Ramp raises $1.85B led by Dragoneer at a $60B valuation
items.parties: Lead: Dragoneer Investment Group; Co-leads: Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, Avenir Growth; Participants include: Capital International, Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, D1 Capital Partners, Greenoaks, ICONIQ, GIC, Coatue, General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and others
items.take: Ramp said it raised a $1.85 billion primary round at a $60 billion valuation, with annualized revenue above $2 billion, positive cash flow and more than 85,000 business customers. The size of the crossover and mutual-fund roster in the round signals that late-stage investors are treating Ramp more like a pre-public company than a venture bet.

items.headline: Labcorp to buy BioReference Health assets from OPKO for $722M plus up to $150M earnout
items.parties: Acquirer: Labcorp; Seller: OPKO Health; Assets: select BioReference Health businesses, including the 4Kscore Test
items.value_text: $722M cash at closing plus up to $150M earnout
items.take: Labcorp will pay $722 million in cash at closing, subject to revenue-based adjustment, plus an earnout of up to $150 million tied to the 4Kscore prostate test, for BioReference's clinical, women's health, urology and corrections testing businesses and more than 80 patient service centers; Labcorp projects about $250 million of first-year revenue. The earnout structure ties about 17% of the maximum price to a single proprietary test, shifting part of the valuation risk back to the seller.
items.correction: Changed the $150 million earnout to 'up to $150 million'; the release describes it as a maximum contingent on 4Kscore Test revenue.

items.headline: Modal raises $750M Series D led by Accel at $15.75B post-money valuation
items.parties: Lead: Accel; Participants: Kleiner Perkins, Menlo Ventures, General Catalyst, Redpoint, Lux Capital, Amplify Partners, Bain Capital Ventures
items.take: Modal said it raised a $750 million Series D led by Accel at a $15.75 billion post-money valuation after crossing $1 billion in annualized run rate, with its sandboxes product alone at a $300 million run rate. The round underlines how quickly capital is moving to inference and agent-execution infrastructure as AI workloads shift from training to production.

items.headline: OrbiMed raises $3B across Private Investments X and Asia Partners VI funds
items.parties: Manager: OrbiMed; Funds: OrbiMed Private Investments X (over $1.9B), OrbiMed Asia Partners VI (over $1B)
items.take: OrbiMed said it raised $3 billion in commitments, with more than $1.9 billion for OrbiMed Private Investments X, targeting U.S. and European life sciences venture deals, and more than $1 billion for OrbiMed Asia Partners VI, targeting healthcare growth equity and venture in Asia. A close of this size for a specialist healthcare manager suggests LPs are still concentrating commitments with established franchises even as biotech fundraising stays selective.

items.headline: OMass Therapeutics raises $310M Series C co-led by Bain, Forbion and Novo
items.parties: Co-leads: Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion, Novo Holdings; Participants: Janus Henderson Investors, SV Health Investors, Jefferson Life Sciences, Syncona, Oxford Science Enterprises, GV, Northpond Ventures, Sanofi Ventures, British Business Bank, University of Oxford
items.take: Oxford-based OMass said its oversubscribed $310 million (£230 million) Series C will fund Phase 2 development of MC2 receptor antagonist OMS1620 in congenital adrenal hyperplasia and ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome and move its SLC15A4 inhibitor toward clinical data in lupus. New backers including public-market investor Janus Henderson alongside specialist life sciences funds give OMass a broader shareholder base heading into mid-stage trials.

items.headline: Stand raises $70M Series C led by Saga Ventures at $1B valuation
items.parties: Lead: Saga Ventures; Participants: Lowercarbon, Eclipse, Equal Ventures, Inspired Capital, Neotribe, Jackson Square Ventures
items.take: Stand, a San Francisco-based home insurer for catastrophe-exposed regions, raised a $70 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation, led by Saga Ventures. Its pitch of pricing individual homes with a physics-based disaster model and discounting resilient properties targets wildfire- and wind-exposed homes, where accurately pricing individual property risk is the core underwriting problem.

items.headline: North.cloud raises $60M Series B led by PeakSpan Capital
items.parties: Lead: PeakSpan Capital; Participants: Litquidity Ventures, Companyon Ventures, Alpaca, Uncommon Denominator, Gaingels, Mana Ventures
items.take: North.cloud, which bills itself as a financial operating system for cloud, AI and data spending, raised a $60 million Series B led by PeakSpan Capital. The round bets that finance teams will want one view across cloud, model and data platforms.

items.headline: CCC Intelligent Solutions to be acquired by GTCR-led group with Elliott for $6.1B
items.parties: Acquirer: Consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR, including Elliott Investment Management L.P. and its affiliates; Target: CCC Intelligent Solutions
items.take: CCC agreed to be taken private for $7.75 per share in cash, an enterprise value of about $6.1 billion and roughly a 44% premium to its unaffected July 9 close, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027 and no financing condition. Pairing a sponsor like GTCR with Elliott shows how activist capital is increasingly sitting on the buy side of software take-privates rather than only agitating from the outside.

items.headline: EQT to buy U.S. real estate manager Stockbridge for $375M plus up to $175M earnout
items.parties: Acquirer: EQT AB; Target: Stockbridge
items.take: EQT will pay a base $375 million in cash from its balance sheet for Stockbridge, which has about $16.5 billion of fee-generating AUM, with up to $175 million more payable over 2027–2030 tied to raising fee-paying commitments in new products. Structuring a third of the potential price as an earnout tied to new fundraising makes this a bet on product expansion in U.S. real estate, not just on buying an existing fee stream.

items.headline: Agilent to buy digital pathology software firm Proscia for $240M plus up to $30M
items.parties: Acquirer: Agilent Technologies; Target: Proscia
items.value_text: $240M cash at closing + up to $30M milestones
items.take: Agilent agreed to acquire Proscia in an all-cash deal valued at $240 million at closing plus up to $30 million in performance milestones, with closing expected early in Agilent's fiscal 2027. Proscia reports trailing twelve-month revenue above $18 million, so the price reflects a strategic premium for an FDA-cleared software layer rather than near-term revenue scale.

items.headline: Labelbox raises more than $100M Series E led by Infinitum Partners
items.parties: Lead: Infinitum Partners; Participants: Wipro Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), B Capital, Tau Ventures, Snowpoint Ventures
items.take: Labelbox said it raised more than $100 million in Series E financing, including equity and a credit facility, led by Infinitum Partners with a16z and B Capital among participants. The undisclosed equity-versus-debt split and the release's lack of a valuation leave the headline figure hard to compare with pure-equity AI rounds.
items.correction: Clarified that the press release, not Labelbox overall, omitted a valuation; the company's blog cited a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation.

items.headline: A.P. Moller Capital fund to buy port operator Portek from Mitsui; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: A.P. Moller Capital – Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II; Seller: Mitsui & Co., Ltd.; Target: Portek International Pte. Ltd.
items.take: A.P. Moller Capital's Emerging Markets Infrastructure Fund II agreed to acquire 100% of Singapore-based Portek, whose terminal interests span Algeria, Gabon, Indonesia, Latvia, Malta and Vietnam, from Mitsui, subject to regulatory and third-party approvals. It is a classic infrastructure-fund carve-out from a trading house, with mid-sized emerging-market terminals moving to a specialist owner.

items.headline: Mueon raises $65M Series A led by Maverick Silicon for AI compute hardware
items.parties: Lead: Maverick Silicon; Participants: Intel Capital, Geodesic Alliances Fund, Oregon Venture Fund, M-Ventures, Wellington Capital, IQT, Defined
items.take: Portland, Oregon-based Mueon raised a $65 million Series A led by Maverick Silicon, with Intel Capital participating, bringing total capital raised to over $80 million to move its stackable Cubelets compute platform toward system validation and production readiness. Strategic money from Intel Capital and IQT in a hardware Series A shows investors widening AI infrastructure bets beyond chips into rack-level density and power.

items.headline: Sirona Medical raises $40M Series D led by Avidity Partners
items.parties: Lead: Avidity Partners; Participants: 8VC, GreatPoint Ventures, KLT Holdings
items.take: Cloud-native radiology software maker Sirona Medical raised a $40 million Series D led by Avidity Partners, and says the round funds its operating plan indefinitely. A late-stage round of this size that the company describes as funding it indefinitely points to a capital-efficiency pitch rather than a growth-at-all-costs raise.

items.headline: AtlasClear signs deal to buy Ark Financial, parent of Dawson James, for up to $24.5M
items.parties: Acquirer: AtlasClear Holdings; Target: Ark Financial Services (parent of Dawson James Securities)
items.take: AtlasClear bought an initial 24.9% of Ark for $2.5 million in cash and a $2.5 million note, and expects to pay $2.4375 million in cash and $13.8125 million in stock for the rest at closing, with up to $3.25 million in deferred consideration, for total consideration of up to $24.5 million. Closing hinges on FINRA approval of Dawson James's continuing membership application, and with roughly two-thirds of the price in stock, existing AtlasClear holders bear dilution.

items.headline: Penske Automotive to be taken private by Penske Corp. and Mitsui at $212 a share
items.parties: Acquirer: Motown Acquisition Corp. (owned by Penske Corporation and Mitsui & Co., Ltd.); Target: Penske Automotive Group, Inc.
items.take: Penske Automotive agreed to be taken private by a buyer owned by Penske Corporation and Mitsui at $212.00 per share in cash, valuing the company at an enterprise value of about $16.3 billion, with Penske expected to hold about 64% and Mitsui 36% after a closing expected in the first quarter of 2027. Beyond regulatory approvals, the deal needs a majority of votes cast by unaffiliated stockholders, a minority-protection condition that gives public holders a genuine say on a controlling-shareholder buyout.

items.headline: Alaunos completes Velaris Therapeutics acquisition alongside $350M private placement
items.parties: Acquirer: Alaunos Therapeutics, Inc.; Target: Velaris Therapeutics, Inc.; Financing lead: Fairmount; Participants: Venrock Healthcare Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price-advised accounts, Wellington, Janus Henderson
items.take: Alaunos Therapeutics completed its acquisition of privately held Velaris Therapeutics, a pulmonary arterial hypertension drug developer, together with an oversubscribed private placement of Series C non-voting convertible preferred stock raising about $350 million in gross proceeds, led by Fairmount; purchase terms were not disclosed. The structure gives Velaris's PAH pipeline a Nasdaq-listed home and funding the company expects to last into 2029, with Fairmount designees set to join the board once stockholders approve the preferred conversion.

items.headline: Volatus Aerospace to buy Lithuanian sensor maker AISPECO for US$10.5M, mostly in stock
items.parties: Acquirer: Volatus Aerospace Inc.; Target: AISPECO Uab
items.value_text: US$10.5M ($3.0M cash, $7.5M stock) plus up to US$2.5M earnout
items.take: Volatus Aerospace agreed to acquire Vilnius-based AISPECO, a maker of airborne sensor systems and flight-management software, for US$10.5 million in base consideration (US$3.0 million cash and US$7.5 million in Volatus shares) plus up to US$2.5 million tied to milestones over three years. The stock-heavy structure lets Volatus add proprietary sensor technology to its defence and aerial intelligence offering while conserving cash; closing is subject to conditions including TSX approval.

items.headline: STERIS to buy specialty surgical products maker Xodus Medical for $2.1B cash
items.parties: Acquirer: STERIS Corporation (subsidiary of STERIS plc); Target: Xodus Medical, Inc. and certain related affiliates; Sellers: Craig E. Kaforey and Mark A. Kaforey
items.take: STERIS signed a purchase agreement to acquire Xodus Medical for $2.1 billion in cash at closing, plus up to $150 million in earnouts tied to 2028 performance, financed primarily with debt and backed by a bridge commitment of up to $2.0 billion from JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. The deal deepens STERIS's push into recurring surgical consumables and is expected to close by December 31, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
items.correction: Headline corrected to describe Xodus Medical as a specialty surgical products maker, as the 8-K states, rather than a surgical safety products maker.

items.headline: Iambic Therapeutics prices $150M Nasdaq IPO at $16 a share
items.parties: Issuer: Iambic Therapeutics, Inc.; Joint book-runners: J.P. Morgan, Jefferies, BofA Securities, Citigroup
items.take: Iambic priced 9,375,000 shares at $16.00 for gross proceeds of $150.0 million, with trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under IAM expected to begin October 15 and an underwriter option for 1,406,250 more shares. The raise gives the clinical-stage company a public-market currency and fresh capital for its pipeline.
items.source_name: Iambic press release (Business Wire, via Stockhouse)

items.headline: Atlas Warehouse Lending prices $750M of 6.25% fixed-to-floating notes due 2032
items.parties: Issuer: Atlas Warehouse Lending Company, L.P. (subsidiary of WHCO Intermediate Holdings L.P.)
items.take: AWLC priced $750 million of senior notes due November 1, 2032, paying 6.250% fixed until November 2031 and then Compounded SOFR plus 2.534%, in a Rule 144A offering expected to close October 21. Proceeds fund assets and general corporate purposes, including possible debt repayment, signaling continued institutional appetite for warehouse-lending platforms.

items.headline: SSR Mining to buy Roxmore Resources for C$6.75 a share, about $464M equity value
items.parties: Acquirer: SSR Mining Inc.; Target: Roxmore Resources Inc.
items.value_text: About $464M equity value (C$6.75/share cash plus SpinCo shares)
items.take: SSR Mining agreed to pay C$6.75 per Roxmore share in cash, a fully diluted equity value of about $464 million and enterprise value of $392 million excluding SpinCo, with Roxmore holders also receiving shares in a spun-out exploration company. The all-cash deal adds the Converse gold project to SSR's development pipeline and is expected to close in Q4 2026.

items.headline: Payward signs deal to buy EU-licensed Saldo Bank; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Payward; Target: Saldo Finance Oy (parent of Saldo Bank UAB)
items.take: Payward signed a definitive agreement to acquire Saldo Bank, a Lithuania-licensed digital bank with passporting across five European markets, with closing expected in 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. An EU banking license would let Payward, whose companies include Kraken, add deposit interest, lending and banking-as-a-service products in Europe.
items.correction: Corrected the target to Saldo Finance Oy, the parent of Saldo Bank UAB, and removed the unsupported word "full" before EU banking license.

items.headline: B&G Foods sells B&M and Joan of Arc bean brands to McCall Farms; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Seller: B&G Foods, Inc.; Acquirer: McCall Farms, Inc.
items.take: B&G Foods said it has sold the B&M and Joan of Arc canned bean brands to McCall Farms and intends to use the net proceeds to repay long-term debt. The divestiture continues B&G's effort to simplify its portfolio around core brands and strengthen its balance sheet.

items.headline: Faraday Future to sell robotics unit to FF EAI Robotics (FFR) in ~$200M stock deal
items.parties: Acquirer: FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc.; Seller: Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc.
items.take: Faraday Future signed definitive agreements to sell its robotics business to FFR for newly issued FFR shares at $2.246 each, valuing the business at about $200 million, after which Faraday Future would hold about 65.7% of FFR on a fully diluted basis. The related-party deal, approved by special committees on both sides, is expected to close by the end of October 2026.

items.headline: ASX-listed Amaero prices $20M U.S. IPO on Nasdaq at $4.25 a share
items.parties: Issuer: Amaero Inc.; Book-runners: Baird (lead), Lake Street
items.take: Amaero priced 4,705,883 shares at $4.25 for roughly $20.0 million in gross proceeds, with Nasdaq Capital Market trading under AMRO expected from October 15 alongside its ASX listing. Up to about $10.0 million is earmarked for capital equipment over the next 12 months.

items.headline: Mubadala Capital completes ~$6.2B acquisition of Clear Channel Outdoor
items.parties: Acquirer: Mubadala Capital (subsidiary of Mubadala Investment Company); Target: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings
items.take: Clear Channel Outdoor said the take-private closed after all applicable regulatory approvals and stockholder approval, and its common stock will be delisted from the NYSE. The close puts a major listed out-of-home ad operator under sovereign-backed private ownership, alongside a leadership change announced the same day.

items.headline: Medtronic accepts 55.0M shares in exchange for all 252.8M MiniMed shares it held
items.parties: Parent: Medtronic; Split-off company: MiniMed Group, Inc.
items.value_text: Undisclosed (share exchange: 252,813,348 MiniMed shares for 55,032,401 Medtronic shares)
items.take: Medtronic said 297,521,390 of its shares were tendered and 55,032,401 accepted at a final proration factor of 18.289133%, in exchange for its entire remaining stake of 252,813,348 MiniMed shares, implying about 4.59 MiniMed shares per Medtronic share. Heavy oversubscription let Medtronic fully exit MiniMed while retiring roughly 55 million of its own shares rather than spinning them out pro rata.

items.headline: Agility to sell Tristar stake to Aegis Logistics at $1.5B enterprise value
items.parties: Seller: Agility Global PLC; Acquirer: Aegis Logistics Limited; Target: Tristar
items.take: Agility said the deal values Tristar at $1.5 billion enterprise value and $882 million equity value, about 6.0x 2025 EBITDA, with closing expected before the end of March 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. Tristar generates $1.4 billion of annual revenue and $257 million of EBITDA, giving India's Aegis a global fuel-logistics footprint across 30+ countries.
items.correction: The release gives Tristar's $1.4 billion revenue and $257 million EBITDA as annual figures without attributing them to 2025; wording corrected.

items.headline: Select Water prices upsized $900M of 7.625% senior notes due 2034
items.parties: Issuer: Select Water Holdings LLC (subsidiary of Select Water Solutions, Inc.)
items.take: The notes were upsized from $800 million, priced at par and are expected to close on October 21, 2026, with proceeds going partly toward the cash consideration for Pilot Water Solutions, repaying the term loan in full and paying down revolver borrowings. A 7.625% coupon locks in long-dated funding for the Pilot deal, and the offering is not contingent on that acquisition closing.
items.source_name: Select Water Solutions press release (PR Newswire)

items.headline: Atlantic Ridge Capital to buy stretch-film maker Paragon Films for about $900M
items.parties: Acquirer: Atlantic Ridge Capital, with Grafine Partners and Paragon management; Target: Paragon Films
items.take: Paragon is the debut investment for New York-based Atlantic Ridge, backed by committed debt financing from UBS Investment Bank, BMO Capital Markets and Santander, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. A roughly $900 million first deal is an unusually large opening bet for a new sponsor on a packaging niche serving more than 20,000 end users.

items.headline: Symbotic acquires German sortation tech firm cellumation; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Symbotic; Target: cellumation GmbH
items.take: Symbotic announced the acquisition of Bremen-based cellumation, maker of the celluveyor modular sortation system, which will keep its name and founder leadership and sell directly and through integrators. The tuck-in adds sortation technology and a larger European base to Symbotic's warehouse automation platform.

items.headline: Freshworks to acquire SaaS management platform Torii; terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Freshworks Inc.; Target: Torii
items.take: Freshworks signed a definitive agreement to buy Torii and expects to close in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions. Torii's app, license and AI-spend tracking extends Freshservice into software spend governance, adding AI-spend tracking to its IT service management suite.

items.headline: Fairfax named strategic buyer for 60.72% of IDBI Bank at about $5.6B
items.parties: Buyer: Fairfax Financial Holdings (via a subsidiary); Contributor: Fairfax India Holdings (IIFL Capital stake); Seller: Government of India; Target: IDBI Bank
items.take: India's government named a Fairfax subsidiary the strategic buyer for a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank at INR 81 a share, about a 23% premium to book value, though no binding agreements are signed and the sale process is not at its final stage. Fairfax also plans to fold its Digit insurance stakes and Fairfax India's IIFL Capital holding into the bank, which would turn IDBI into a broader financial-services platform if regulators sign off.
items.correction: Fairfax India Holdings is a co-announcer contributing its IIFL Capital stake, not a buyer of the 60.72% stake; parties corrected.

items.headline: BlackRock's HPS buys WCAS stake, valued near $2.8B, in Humana CenterWell clinics JV
items.parties: Buyer: funds and accounts managed by HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock; Seller: WCAS; Partner: Humana (CenterWell)
items.take: BlackRock will take majority ownership of a new joint venture running nearly 150 CenterWell Senior Primary Care clinics by acquiring WCAS's equity, valued at about $2.8 billion, with closing expected in the fourth quarter. The new structure has no put option, which Humana says should significantly reduce balance-sheet liabilities while it keeps a right to buy clinics back from 2028.

items.headline: Cipher Digital prices $850M of 0.00% convertible notes due 2032
items.parties: Issuer: Cipher Digital Inc.
items.take: Cipher Digital priced $850 million of zero-coupon converts due 2032 at an initial conversion price of about $15.31, a 35% premium, for net proceeds of about $835.1 million, of which about $89.7 million goes to capped calls. The rest funds the Barber Lake project and HPC build-out, while a concurrent swap is expected to retire about $165.9 million of 2030 notes for roughly 40.7 million shares.
items.correction: Clarified that the exchange of 2030 notes is expected, not completed, per the release.

items.headline: Brookdale to buy 30 leased communities from Welltower for $290M
items.parties: Acquirer: Brookdale Senior Living; Seller: Welltower
items.take: Brookdale will pay $290 million for 30 leased communities with 1,152 units, cutting about $17.8 million of 2027 cash rent, after closing a separate $157 million purchase of 17 communities on September 30. Together the two deals cover 47 communities and move Brookdale's owned share of units toward nearly 80%, reducing the share of its portfolio held under leases.
items.correction: Corrected the closing date of the separate 17-community purchase to September 30, not the same day as the Welltower announcement.

items.headline: Reach Security raises more than $50M Series B led by Top Tier Capital Partners
items.parties: Lead: Top Tier Capital Partners; Participants: Ballistic Ventures, In-Q-Tel, M12 (Microsoft's Venture Fund), existing investors
items.take: Reach Security, whose AI reads the live configuration of customers' existing security tools to close attack paths, will spend the money on product, integrations, international expansion and U.S. enterprise and federal growth. In-Q-Tel and Microsoft's M12 on the cap table give it credibility in the government and Microsoft-centric enterprise segments it is targeting.

items.headline: Porch Group and its reciprocal to buy insurer Allied Trust for $200M including deferred consideration
items.parties: Acquirers: Porch Group and the Reciprocal it manages; Target: Allied Trust
items.value_text: $200M total ($150M combined base price plus $50M deferred), cash and stock
items.take: The Reciprocal pays a $55 million base price plus $50 million deferred for the carrier, while Porch pays $95 million for the managing agency and captive reinsurer, which Porch puts at under four times expected first-year adjusted EBITDA. The deal adds Louisiana and about $200 million of written premium, deepening Porch's exposure to Gulf and Southeast homeowners markets.
items.correction: Corrected the headline and value text: the combined base price is $150M ($55M + $95M); the $200M total includes $50M of deferred consideration.

items.headline: Salience Labs raises $125M Series B led by Bullhound for optical AI switches
items.parties: Lead: Bullhound Capital; Participants: AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, SBI Group, Hudson River Trading, British Business Bank, Applied Ventures, Oxford Science Enterprises, Cambridge Innovation Capital, Silicon Catalyst Ventures
items.take: Backing from AMD Ventures and Intel Capital puts chipmaker money behind optical circuit switching, which aims to cut the power and latency of moving data between AI accelerators. The round funds volume manufacturing and 128- and 256-port products, a sign that datacenter networking is drawing capital alongside compute itself.
items.source_name: Cambridge Innovation Capital (Salience Labs press release)

items.headline: Workday to acquire agentic identity platform C1.ai (ConductorOne); terms undisclosed
items.parties: Acquirer: Workday; Target: C1.ai (ConductorOne, Inc.); Advisors: BofA Securities, Orrick (Workday); Qatalyst, Ashurst Perkins Coie (C1.ai)
items.take: Workday is buying identity-governance software that grants and revokes system access for both people and AI agents, extending its HR system of record toward controlling what agents can do. As enterprises deploy AI agents, governing their access is emerging as a new control point for enterprise software platforms.

items.headline: SentinelOne prices $1.25B of 0.00% convertible notes due 2031
items.parties: Issuer: SentinelOne
items.take: The zero-coupon notes convert at about $31.21 a share, a 30% premium, and roughly $150 million of proceeds goes to buying back stock from note purchasers alongside $131.6 million of capped calls. Pairing the converts with a buyback and a capped call at a 100% premium is designed to raise cash at no running interest cost while limiting dilution.

items.headline: IonQ to acquire zero-trust security firm Elisity for up to $1.3B in stock
items.parties: Acquirer: IonQ; Target: Elisity
items.value_text: Up to $1.3B all stock, incl. up to $150M earnout
items.take: IonQ is again using its stock as acquisition currency, this time to add network access-control software that governs users, devices, workloads and AI agents. The deal widens IonQ's security pitch beyond quantum hardware and networking, with closing targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026.

items.headline: Bumble agrees to $1.3B all-cash sale to Ithaca Holdings at $6.05 a share
items.parties: Acquirer: Ithaca Holdings; Target: Bumble Inc.; Advisors: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Davis Polk (Bumble special committee); Kirkland & Ellis, KKR Capital Markets (Ithaca); Wachtell Lipton (Whitney Wolfe Herd); Simpson Thacher (Blackstone)
items.take: The $6.05 per-share price is about a 138% premium to Bumble's unaffected October 9 close, and written consent from Blackstone affiliates and Whitney Wolfe Herd already delivers the shareholder approval. The take-private hands the dating app to a holding company whose co-CEOs become Bumble's co-CEOs, a bet that a long-term private owner can reshape a mature consumer app away from quarterly scrutiny.

items.headline: AT&T to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2B cash
items.parties: Seller: AT&T; Target: AT&T Mexico; Buyers: Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings
items.value_text: $2B cash at closing, plus contractual and contingent benefits
items.take: The sale ends AT&T's wireless push into Mexico and, per the company, supports its capital allocation toward U.S. fiber and wireless. For Mexico's market, pairing Televisa's fixed broadband base with a national mobile network creates a combined fixed-mobile challenger, subject to Mexican regulatory approval.

items.headline: Galderma to buy ZO Skin Health from Blackstone-backed owners for $1.5B
items.parties: Acquirer: Galderma; Target: ZO Skin Health; Sellers: ZO shareholders including funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and the Obagi family; Advisors: Lazard, JP Morgan, Ropes & Gray (Galderma); Raymond James, Citi, Weil, Gotshal & Manges, Paul Weiss (ZO and Blackstone)
items.take: Galderma is paying an enterprise value of $1.5 billion for a physician-dispensed skincare brand with about $330 million of trailing net sales, roughly 4.5 times sales, funded with cash and bank loans. The deal adds a daily-regimen line alongside its procedure-focused aesthetics business and shows strategic buyers still paying up for scaled, professional-channel skincare assets.
